visual_source_files.evidence: 公开仓库 main@c30196a1d7e9a33be3f8827e2fc32a6067b83131；format_settings 设置 font/axes/tick/legend rcParams，默认 fs=12、save_dpi=300、lw=1.5、ms=5、axlw=1.5，并提供 viridis；未见 Figure 1–3 调用。
公开仓库 main@c30196a1d7e9a33be3f8827e2fc32a6067b83131；包含通用 loss/norm/accuracy plotting utilities（含 #c82423、#2878b5 和 viridis），没有 Figure 1–3 的组合、PCA、attention heatmap 或 caption 源。

source_acquisition.search_note: PDF 首页、正文和 References 只有 arXiv/OpenReview 链接，没有作者明确的 GitHub/project URL。gh 的完整标题、方法词、作者词和 arXiv ID 搜索唯一严格匹配 MiracleLin001/Transformer_Training_Dynamics；README 明确列出本文完整标题及 arXiv:2605.01199。gh api 读取该仓库树后未发现 paper/、.tex、.tikz、.pgf、.ipynb、figures/ 或 Figure-specific source；train.py 引用了树中不存在的 draw_condense_heatmap。gh search code 的 Paper-Notes/Paper-Notes-en 命中是读书笔记，不是作者视觉源。因此仅保留通用 plotting/style 文件，所有图内数值均按 PDF 渲染估计记录。

paper_style.palette_strategy: Figure 1 使用框线/阶段色和蓝灰 loss 曲线；Figure 2–3 使用 viridis 连续色带表达矩阵强度，再用 token 离散色和浅色阶段带表达类别与时间阶段。没有 uncertainty palette。
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: 三个视觉对象的图内曲线、矩阵、坐标和标签均来自 PDF 嵌入栅格；Figure 1 是 3500×1145 RGB+mask，Figure 2/3 是 RGB 或 indexed 栅格分片。caption、正文和公式是独立 PDF 字体对象，因此页面整体是 mixed，但对象本身是 raster。
paper_style.style_consistency: 三条 caption 采用相同的斜体 Figure label、粗体标题和括号分面说明；Figure 2/3 共享 viridis 语义与小型无衬线图内字，但 Figure 1 的概念框配色和字号更大，token 色在跨图/跨语料间不完全固定。

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1. Overview of the setting and the focus–dilution training pattern. (Left) Sequences are generated by a Markov chain with stationary distribution π. We extract dataset S0, S1, S2 from the training set, which differ only in the identity of the final token in each sequence. (Right) The loss curves exhibit four stages: initial condensation, attention growth, attention dilution, and the emergence of a new direction.

color.semantic_mapping: 紫/红/蓝框区分 Phenomena、Data、Architecture；蓝、绿、橙、棕分别标记 Stage I–IV；深/中/浅蓝灰标记 S0/S1/S2 loss，灰色虚/点线为 Bigram/Unigram baselines；框内矩阵用蓝青强度表示参数快照。

plot_grammar.legend_placement: inside lower-left of the right Phenomena chart

encodings.x: Step 0–2500 in the mini loss chart; Data/Architecture boxes have no axis.
encodings.y: Train Loss in the mini chart; equations and boxes otherwise have no numeric axis.
encodings.color: Stage I–IV, S0/S1/S2 and Bigram/Unigram baselines; blue-green matrix intensity.
encodings.shape: Open circles mark milestones on the loss curves; rounded boxes and arrow junctions organize the schematic.
encodings.line: Solid S0/S1/S2 curves; dashed S1 Bigram; dotted Unigram; gray connectors from loss milestones to matrix snapshots.
encodings.facet: Data and Architecture on the left; Phenomena/stage timeline and loss chart on the right.
encodings.text: Data/Architecture/Phenomena headers, stage names, W0/WQ/WK/W1 labels, equations, and mechanism callouts.

figures.data_and_statistics: The left schematic defines Markov data and three datasets S0/S1/S2 that differ by final token; the right plot is a qualitative loss trajectory with three dataset curves and two reference baselines. No aggregation, run count, uncertainty, error bar, or failure value is shown; matrix insets are illustrative parameter snapshots rather than numeric tables.
figures.evidence_relation: Connects §2.2–§2.3 Markov data and one-layer architecture to §3 initial condensation, attention growth, dilution, and new direction, then previews the synthetic measurements in Figure 2. It is the overview interface for the theory-to-experiment chain, not a standalone estimate.
design_strengths: Places data construction, model interface, stage sequence, and observable loss pattern in one cross-column map.
Uses stage names plus colored backgrounds/curves and milestone circles to make the causal reading order visible.
Caption explains left/right roles and states the four-stage finding without requiring the surrounding paragraph.
design_weaknesses: Rasterized equations, matrix insets, and small chart labels are difficult to search or enlarge.
Stage colors carry more information than shape/line redundancy, so grayscale or color-vision-limited reading loses distinctions.
Matrix snapshots have no numeric scale and the mini curve is schematic, so the object cannot support quantitative comparison.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a three-block cross-column overview—data → architecture → stage timeline—with a small loss/transition plot whose named stages map directly to later mechanism panels.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2. Empirical focus–dilution cycle. (A) Loss curves for S0, S1, S2, accompanied by cosine-similarity matrices for (W0, WQ, WK, W1). (B) PCA of embeddings reveals one-directional growth (Stage I & II), retraction during dilution (Stage III), and expansion into new directions (Stage IV). (C) Attention maps transition from focus to dilution. Between steps 350 and 550, the attention given to the first token by all query pairs increases synchronously. Afterward, the first token focuses attention on itself, while other tokens reduce their attention towards it. (D1) Attention entropy; (D2), (D3) The embedding norm and the norm of perpendicular component onto the first token.

color.semantic_mapping: viridis 紫→蓝→青→绿→黄表达 cosine/attention 强度；蓝、绿、橙、棕表达 token 0–3 轨迹；米色/浅灰绿竖带表达 Stage 1–4；深/中/浅蓝灰表达 S0/S1/S2 loss。

plot_grammar.legend_placement: inside A lower-left; inside B and D panels near lower-right/right

encodings.x: A: Step on a log axis (10¹–10⁴); B: linear PCA coordinate; C/D: linear Step positions.
encodings.y: A: Train Loss linear; B: linear PCA coordinate; C: Key Token categorical; D: linear entropy/norm.
encodings.color: Stage bands, S0/S1/S2 loss, token 0–3 trajectories, and viridis heatmap intensity.
encodings.shape: Filled/open circles distinguish current/previous PCA points; heatmap/matrix cells encode values by position and color.
encodings.line: Loss and diagnostic trajectories are solid; A includes dashed/ dotted baselines; B includes a dashed diagonal reference and dotted trajectory segments.
encodings.facet: A; B1–B4 stage windows; C1–C4 query-token maps; D1 entropy, D2 embedding norm, D3 perpendicular norm.
encodings.text: Panel labels, stage/window titles, query-token headings, axis labels, legends, and shared heatmap colorbar.

figures.data_and_statistics: A compares S0/S1/S2 train-loss trajectories and cosine-similarity matrices for W0/WQ/WK/W1 at stage anchors; B projects embedding snapshots to PCA; C displays query-wise attention over tokens and steps; D traces entropy, W0 norm, and perpendicular-component norm. These are single training trajectories with selected checkpoints; no replicate aggregation, denominator, error bar, interval, band, or failure count is provided.
figures.evidence_relation: Operationalizes the four stages previewed by Figure 1 and §3: A tests condensation and loss transitions, B tests one-directional growth/retraction/new directions, C tests focus-to-dilution redistribution, and D supplies entropy/norm diagnostics. Appendix E.2 (pp. 54–55) defines the cosine heatmap and PCA procedures; no ablation or baseline replacement is shown.
design_strengths: A/B/C/D align loss anchors, parameter geometry, attention redistribution, and diagnostic norms into one stage-aware mechanism map.
Stage bands, panel titles, milestone connectors, and previous/current markers provide a visible temporal scaffold.
C uses a shared viridis colorbar and the caption states the 350–550-step transition and its interpretation.
design_weaknesses: Twelve dense panels, repeated legends, matrix insets, and tiny token labels are hard to read at double-column width.
A uses log Step while C/D use linear Step, requiring an axis-scale switch within one figure.
Single-trajectory plots lack run-level uncertainty and cannot distinguish a general mechanism from a particular optimization path.
figures.reusable_pattern: For stage-structured training dynamics, use the sequence loss/phase anchor → geometry → attention map → diagnostic norms, with each row tied to one theoretical transition and a shared intensity legend.

evidence.label: Figure 2 (A, B1–B4, C1–C4, D1–D3) and caption; 200 dpi rendered page/object crop

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3. Experimental results on real-world datasets. (A) Results on WikiText. (A1) The attention evolution of the medium-frequency token ’continue’ given the input sequence [the, comma, whitespace, ter, end, continue]. The attention scores exhibit a distinct four-phase transition: dilution → focus on the high-frequency whitespace → secondary dilution → final focus on continue itself. (A2) The evolution of ∥W0∥2 for selected tokens. The dominant whitespace token shows continuous growth, while other tokens display a clear retraction. (B) Results on TinyStories. We observe similar dynamics using the input sequence [the, comma, a, full, been], mirroring the phenomena in (A). (C) Visualization of attention shifts. The evolution of attention for a single test sample across different training steps, with tokens exhibiting self-attention scores ≥ 0.75 highlighted.

color.semantic_mapping: viridis 紫→蓝→青→绿→黄表达 attention 强度；A2/B2 用蓝、绿、橙、红、紫、棕区分 token norm 曲线；红色 token 标签/对角标记强调 self-attention ≥ 0.75。

plot_grammar.legend_placement: inside upper-left of A2 and B2; colorbars at heatmap right edges

encodings.x: A1/B1 token categories; A2/B2 linear Steps; C1–C4 token/category columns.
encodings.y: A1/B1 linear Training Steps; A2/B2 linear Norm of W0; C1–C4 token/key categories.
encodings.color: Viridis attention values; token-specific line colors; red token labels/diagonal highlights for self-attention threshold.
encodings.shape: No line markers; heatmap cell position and lower-triangular matrix structure encode token pairs.
encodings.line: A2/B2 solid norm curves; no line-style distinction among token series; B2 has a gray horizontal reference line.
encodings.facet: WikiText A1/A2, TinyStories B1/B2, and attention snapshots C1–C4 at ini/1400/2200/15000 steps.
encodings.text: Query headings, input tokens, step titles, token legends, rotated/multiline token labels, and per-panel colorbars.

figures.data_and_statistics: A1/B1 show selected-query attention heatmaps over training steps; A2/B2 show selected-token embedding norms; C1–C4 show one test sample at four checkpoints with self-attention scores ≥ 0.75 highlighted. The real-data evidence is selected-token/selected-sample and qualitative; no corpus-wide aggregation, replicate count, uncertainty, or failure tally is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Extends Figure 2's focus–dilution/retraction signatures from synthetic Markov data to WikiText and TinyStories. A1/A2 and B1/B2 support the claimed qualitative transfer; C visualizes the attention-shift interpretation. The object is a robustness/generalization signal, not a controlled non-Markov comparison or quantitative benchmark.
design_strengths: Pairs attention heatmaps with norm trajectories for each real corpus and adds four temporal attention snapshots.
Caption provides concrete token sequences, four-phase interpretation, training-step context, and the ≥0.75 highlighting rule.
The same viridis intensity convention keeps attention maps visually comparable to Figure 2.
design_weaknesses: C token labels and multiple colorbars are dense and difficult to read at double-column size.
A/B token sets and line-color assignments are not globally identical, so cross-corpus comparison requires the local legends.
One sample and selected tokens do not establish corpus-wide robustness; color-only token distinctions degrade in grayscale.
figures.reusable_pattern: For qualitative real-data transfer, place selected-token heatmaps, norm trajectories, and checkpoint attention matrices on one page, and state the exact input sequence and threshold in the caption.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 gives the data/architecture/four-stage map; Figure 2 measures the synthetic mechanism through loss, parameter geometry, attention maps, entropy and norms; Figure 3 transfers selected signatures to WikiText and TinyStories.
cross_object_system.caption_system: All three captions use an italic Figure label followed by a bold title and parenthetical panel keys. Each caption states setup/encoding and a main observation; none defines uncertainty, denominator, run count, or an appendix pointer.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: No tables occur in the 55-page PDF, so there is no table-header hierarchy, unit/direction convention, best-value highlighting, cost column, or failure column to audit.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 1 is the method/theory interface, Figure 2 is the main mechanism evidence, and Figure 3 is the selected real-data extension. No component ablation, baseline substitution, sensitivity sweep, or failure matrix is present.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: All three visual objects are in the main body. Appendix E.2 (pp. 54–55) defines the cosine heatmap and PCA operations used in Figure 2; Appendices B–D carry proof details but contain no figures or tables.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Body/captions use Times/Computer Modern-style serif and math fonts; embedded figure labels use small sans-serif text. Figure 2 and Figure 3 are similar in small-panel scale, while Figure 1 uses larger conceptual labels.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Viridis maps attention/cosine magnitude across Figures 2–3, but token line colors and stage backgrounds are not a fully fixed global mapping. Figure 1's stage hues partly anticipate Figure 2; color carries primary semantics and is not grayscale-safe.

most_reusable_patterns: Cross-column data → architecture → stage-timeline overview with a caption that states left/right reading order.
Stage-aware loss/geometry/attention/diagnostic panel chain that assigns each theoretical transition an observable signature.
Selected-token heatmap + norm curve + checkpoint matrix for qualitative real-data transfer, with exact token sequence and threshold in the caption.
highest_value_objects: Figure 2 (p. 7): 12-panel synthetic mechanism map linking loss, cosine matrices, PCA, attention, entropy and norms.
Figure 3 (p. 8): real-corpus qualitative extension across WikiText and TinyStories.
failure_patterns: Rasterized composite figures put many legends, colorbars, token labels and scales into small double-column panels.
Figure 2 mixes log and linear Step axes; Figure 3 changes token sets/color assignments across datasets.
All results are single trajectories or selected samples without replicate-level uncertainty, denominator, or failure summaries.
No tables, benchmark comparison, efficiency/cost view, or ablation is available.
The strict-title public repository lacks Figure-specific plotting and LaTeX sources, preventing source-exact visual reproduction.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: Figure 1 draws the four-stage causal map, Figure 2 closes the synthetic mechanism with aligned multi-readout timelines, and Figure 3 offers selected real-data snapshots while leaving quantitative uncertainty outside the visual system.
